Winner of The Voice Season 29 Alexia Jayy won Season 29 of The Voice, subtitled Battle of Champions, on Tuesday, April 14, 2026. Guided by coach Adam Levine, the 31-year-old singer from Mobile, Alabama, became the first African-American female to win in the show's history. Season 29 Finale Results The results were determined by a studio audience comprised of former The Voice artists and superfans. ArtistCoachWinnerAlexia JayyWinnerAdam LevineRunner-upLiv CiaraRunner-upKelly ClarksonThird PlaceLucas WestThird PlaceJohn LegendFourth PlaceMikenley BrownFourth PlaceKelly Clarkson Winning Highlights Coach Adam Levine's Milestone: This marked Levine's fourth overall win as a coach and his first since Season 9. It tied him with Kelly Clarkson for the second-most winning coach, behind Blake Shelton. Finale Performances: During the finale, Jayy performed Patti LaBelle's "Lady Marmalade" and Adele's "One and Only". She also performed a duet of "Sunday Morning" with Levine. New Music: Following her victory, Jayy released her single "Rent Free" on April 15, 2026. Prizes: Along with the title, Jayy received her own home recording studio and a full year of internet and mobile services provided by Xfinity.
